title_en: The town that was secure and content
notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu are left for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. A parable or similitude is not a dated event and is not placed in any order: the chapter states only what the ayat present as a similitude, what it is likened to, and what the ayat themselves say. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

claims.statement_en: God struck a similitude: a town that was secure and at ease, its provision coming to it in plenty from every place; it disbelieved in the favours of God, so God made it taste the garment of hunger and fear because of what they used to do.
A messenger from among them had come to them and they called him a liar, so the punishment seized them while they were wrongdoers.

chapters.summary_md: God struck a similitude of a town that was secure and at ease, with its provision coming in plenty from every place [c1]. It disbelieved in the favours of God, and God made it taste the garment of hunger and fear [c1].
chapters.body_md: God struck a similitude: a town that was secure and at ease, its provision coming to it in plenty from every place [c1]. It disbelieved in the favours of God, so God made it taste the garment of hunger and fear because of what they used to do [c1]. A messenger from among them had come to them and they called him a liar [c2]. The punishment seized them while they were wrongdoers [c2].
chapters.deep_md: The first ayah describes the town as secure and supplied, and then at the point of hunger and fear [c1]. The next ayah says that a messenger from among them had come and was called a liar before the punishment seized them [c2]. The ayat do not name the town, the messenger or the punishment [c1][c2].
chapters.kids_md: God struck a similitude of a town that was secure and at ease, with its provision coming in plenty [c1]. The town disbelieved in the favours of God, and God made it taste hunger and fear [c1]. A messenger from among them had come, and they called him a liar [c2].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat set security and plenty beside disbelief in the favours of God, and then hunger and fear [c1]. Another reading is that the ayat link the seizing by the punishment with calling the messenger a liar [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: which town is meant, where or when it was, or who the messenger was; none is named.
- Not established: whether the similitude describes a particular past town or is an example.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later commentary links the town to a particular place; this draft does not repeat or vouch for it.
- The verb kafarat in 16:112 can be read as disbelieved or as was ungrateful; this draft keeps disbelieved in the favours of God and leaves the sense open.
- The ayah itself says that God struck a similitude (mathal).

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: none identified; a scholar should say whether any should be linked to these ayat.
The sense of kafarat and the favours of God and of the garment of hunger and fear is for a scholar to decide.
